advisory.finding: store_status()'s docstring states 'Never raises', but the function deliberately re-raises RemovedInputError (a BaseException) when TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR is set, so GET /health can return HTTP 500. This contradicts the docstring and the stated design ('a health probe must not be able to fail (or block)'), and — because /health is both the container HEALTHCHECK and readiness probe under `restart: always` — reintroduces the very crash-loop the report-not-fail design was built to avoid, for that one retired-input case.
scenarios: A box still setting the retired TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR env var: /health raises 500, container HEALTHCHECK fails, and with restart: always the container enters a restart loop.

An equivalent rewrite (e.g. `not st.get("present") and st.get("expected")`, or refactoring the embedded python into a helper) would fail the assertion despite identical behavior — Rule 4 change-detector

The embedded classifier at infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:711-716 (print 'missing' if expected and not present else 'ok') is never fed a real JSON body and asserted to emit 'missing'/'ok'; the test cannot detect a regression in the parse (e.g. wrong key name, or the `or {}` fallthrough) that keeps the same literal string present

advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the embedded python into a small script or invoke it via subprocess with piped JSON stdin, asserting stdout is 'missing'/'ok' for each case (including the mixed-version no-`store`-key body and a malformed body).

evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:150 `return {"path": path, "present": os.path.isdir(path), "expected": expected}`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:392 `- gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` (a named volume mount, so the target dir always exists in the container)
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:369 `-v "gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets"` (blue-green container mounts the same volume at the same target)

infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:9-13 — a fresh single-branch clone is NOT a usable store: `.env-id` is git-ignored, so the clone lacks it and every write fails 'ticket system not initialized'; store usability is the `.env-id` marker, not directory existence

Dockerfile.mcp:78-100 — the clone+converge is SOFT failure posture (deferred on missing PAT/clone error), which produces exactly a present-directory / no-usable-store state that isdir() reports as present=True
advisory.finding: The /health store-presence signal keys on directory existence (os.path.isdir), but the MCP container always bind-mounts the named volume gerrit_mcp_tickets at REBAR_TRACKER_DIR (/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets), so that directory always exists — meaning `present` is True even for an un-converged/empty store, which is precisely the storeless failure mode (mobile-groovy-badger) the change was built to detect. The autodeploy gate `expected AND not present` therefore never fires in the deployed compose/blue-green topology.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute presence from the store marker the write path actually gates on, e.g. `present = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, ".env-id"))`, so a mounted-but-un-converged store (deferred clone/ensure) reports present=False and the autodeploy `expected AND not present` gate fires.

evidence: tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py:280: `sources = [pkg / "mcp_server.py", pkg / "_mcp_health.py"]`
The scan only iterates `sources`; a broad except in e.g. `build_server`'s callee or `_mcp_auth` on the boot path is out of scope and produces no failure.
Docstring at :273-277 acknowledges this: "if the handler moved again, extend this list" — a manual maintenance burden that is itself the fail-open.
advisory.finding: The relocated contract-guard test scans a hardcoded two-file allowlist (`mcp_server.py`, `_mcp_health.py`); a broad `except Exception`/`except BaseException` added to any OTHER boot-path module is never scanned, so an unguarded broad handler outside those two files passes this check invisibly — the guard cannot distinguish "boot path is clean" from "the unguarded except is in a file I don't look at."

evidence: tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py:109 `assert 'st.get("expected") and not st.get("present")' in autodeploy`

The asserted string is the exact Python boolean expression at infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:715; reordering to `not st.get("present") and st.get("expected")`, adjusting whitespace, or extracting a helper is behavior-preserving yet fails this assertion (refactoring-violation criterion)

The grepped token is implementation logic, not a canonical identifier read by a non-human consumer, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply; the test never executes the gate, so it cannot catch a gate that promotes a storeless container (regression-blindness criterion)

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 151 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug d9ab-7b5e-fe4c-4ff4 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan d9ab-7b5e-fe4c-4ff4` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review d9ab-7b5e-fe4c-4ff4` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan d9ab-7b5e-fe4c-4ff4 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
